title: “JESUS MARVELED.”
paragraphs: “JESUS MARVELED.”
At a Roman soldier.

Not a prophet.
Not a priest.
Not one of the Twelve.

A man in uniform.
A man trained to kill.
A representative of the empire crushing Israel’s neck.

And Jesus…
marveled.
Why?
Stay with me.
In Gospel of Matthew 8, a centurion approaches Jesus. A commander over a hundred soldiers. Authority in his voice. Steel in his spine.
But when he speaks, it isn’t command.
It’s compassion.
“Lord, my servant lies paralyzed at home, suffering terribly.”

Did you catch it?
A Roman officer… pleading for a servant.

Not demanding.
Not threatening.
Pleading.
Jesus answers, “I will come and heal him.”
And this is where heaven leans in.
The centurion replies:
“Lord, I am not worthy to have You come under my roof. But only say the word, and my servant will be healed.”
Stop.

A Gentile soldier saying he’s unworthy.
While Israel’s religious elite argued about worthiness every day.
He continues:
“For I too am a man under authority…”
Under.
That’s the word.

He understood something many church people still miss:
Authority flows from submission.
He saw in Jesus not just a healer… but a King.
He recognized divine authority wrapped in dusty sandals.
And Scripture says Jesus marveled.

There are only two times in the Gospels where Jesus marvels.
One at unbelief (Mark 6:6).
Here — at faith.
“Truly, I tell you, with no one in Israel have I found such faith.”
Can you feel the tension?

The outsiders are leaning in.
The insiders are missing it.
A pagan soldier sees what the covenant people overlook.
And then the promise explodes:
“Many will come from east and west and recline at table with Abraham…”
That’s the Gospel breaking through the border wall.
This is bigger than one healing.
This is about access.

The centurion didn’t ask for a touch.
He didn’t demand a sign.
He didn’t negotiate terms.
He trusted the Word.
“Only say the word.”
And Jesus did.
And at that very hour, the servant was healed.
Let me speak to you straight.

You don’t need proximity.
You need faith.

You don’t need perfect pedigree.
You need surrender.

You don’t need to clean up your résumé.
You need to recognize authority.

Some of you feel too far.
Too pagan.
Too stained by your past.
But this Roman soldier stepped across every cultural line and said, “Lord… I am not worthy.”
That’s where real faith begins.

Not hype.
Not performance.
Humble trust in the authority of Christ.
And here’s the scandal of grace:
The One with all authority became the Servant who went to a cross.
The King who commands armies allowed nails to command His hands.
Why?
Because we were the paralyzed ones.

Sin had us pinned.
Shame had us shackled.
Death had us scheduled.
And Jesus didn’t just say a word from a distance.
He came near.

He bore our sin.
He took our judgment.
He rose in authority over death itself.
Now the invitation stands:
Believe the Word.
Trust the King.
Submit to His authority — and you will find life under it.

Faith is not loud.
It is surrendered.

And when heaven marvels…
it’s not at talent.
It’s at trust.
Will Jesus marvel at your faith?

Bow the knee.
Trust His Word.
Receive His grace.
